info.title: ControlUp for Desktops
info.description:
This is a working document that details the supported Edge DX API endpoints which can be used by things
                    such as external applications, scripts, or services. If an endpoint is documented, efforts will be made
                    to try and prevent breaking changes as the API evolves.

FilterField.name: filters[0][field]
FilterField.description:
Filters the returned data based on the specified field name. This parameter must be used in combination with `filters[0][type]` and `filters[0][value]` to define a filter condition.
You can add multiple filter conditions by changing the integer in the parameter names (for example, `filters[1][field]`).</br></br>

FilterType.name: filters[0][type]
FilterType.description:
The type of filter used in corresponding filter condition. The type of filter you can use depends on the data type of the field.

`<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `<=`, or `>` are used to filter numbers and dates.
`boolean` is used to filter boolean fields.
`like` is used to filter text fields.

FilterValue.name: filters[0][value]
FilterValue.description:
The value used in the corresponding filter condition. The value you can use depends on the filter type.

If you are filtering a date or text field, enter a string. If you are filtering a number field, enter a number. If you are filtering a boolean field, enter a boolean. If you are filtering a text field, you can use * as a wildcard, or begin the string with !! to exclude items that contain the string.

SorterField.name: sorters[0][field]
SorterField.description:
Sorts the returned data based on the specified field name. This parameter must be used in combination with `sorters[0][dir]` to set the sort order.
You can sort by more than one field by changing the integer in the parameter names (for example, `sorters[1][field]`). Sorters with a lower integer are applied first.</br></br>

SorterDir.name: sorters[0][dir]
SorterDir.description: The sort order for the corresponding field. Set to `asc` for ascending, or `desc` for descending.

500.description: Something went wrong at the API service.

enabled.description: Indicates if the alert is enabled.

platform.description:
OS platform. This determines which scripts are available to select as a followup action when the alert is triggered. This does not determine which devices can trigger the script. 
* 0 - No platform selected
* 1 - Windows
* 2 - macOS
* 3 - Linux
* 4 - ChromeOS

servicenow_raise_incident.description: Indicates if the Alert raises a ServiceNow ticket when it activates. "true" means that a ticket is raised.

servicenow_ticket_type.description:
Type of ServiceNow ticket.
* `1` = Incident
* `2` = Event

servicenow_impact.description:
Impact level for the ServiceNow ticket.
* `1` = High
* `2` = Medium
* `3` = Low

servicenow_urgency.description:
Urgency level for the ServiceNow ticket.
* `1` = High
* `2` = Medium
* `3` = Low

servicenow_autoclose_interval.description: Auto-close interval for the ServiceNow ticket in seconds.

description.example: Description of my first alert goes here

index.description: Index associated with the alert. The alerts conditions (located in `filters) must be based off of fields in the data index.

filters.description: List of conditions for the alert to activate. Multiple conditions are combined using AND operators.

type.description: Type of comparison. Note that if you are filtering on a string field, you must use the "like" filter type.

value.description: Value to compare against. Numbers can be passed as strings.

results_threshold.description: The number of times that the conditions must be met within the time window (`results_threshold_seconds`) for the trigger to activate.

results_threshold_seconds.description: The length of time in seconds that the alert system searches back to check whether the alert's activation conditions were met.

retrigger_interval.description: The minimum duration between subsequent alert activations. If the retrigger interval duration has not passed since the last alert activation, then the alert won't activate even if all conditions are met.

severity.description:
Severity level of the alert.
* 1 - Informational
* 2 - Low
* 3 - Medium
* 4 - High
* 5 - Critical

webhook_url.description: URL for a webhook to be triggered.

script_id.description: ID of a system script to run on devices that trigger the alert. You can use [GET /scripts](list-all-scripts) to see script IDs.

user_script_id.description: ID of a user script to run on devices that trigger the alert. You can use [GET /scripts](list-all-scripts) to see script IDs.

survey_id.description: ID of an on-demand survey to run on devices that trigger the alert. You can use [GET /surveys](get-surveys) to see survey IDs.

email_addresses.description: A semicolon-separated list of email addresses to receive an email when the alert triggers.

rows.description: An array of the rows (documents) in the data index. Each entry in the array is a different document. The data in each document depends on the index being retrieved.

rows_available.description: The total number of rows that are stored in the data index.

page_size.description: The number of rows that are able to be displayed per page of results.

start_row.description: The first row that can be returned on the current page.

end_row.description: The last row that can be returned on the current page.

mappings.description: Information about the fields (columns) in the index. Each entry in the array represents a different field.

_created.description: The UTC date and time that the custom report was created.

_updated.description: The UTC date and time that the custom report was last updated.

_associated_id.description: ID of the user who created the custom report.

index.description: The name of the index that contains the data for the custom report.

name.description: The name of the custom report.

is_public.description: If true, the custom report is available to all users in your organization. If false, it is only available to the user who created it.

type.description: The data type of the field.

_created.description: The UTC date and time that the UI state was created.

_updated.description: The UTC date and time that the UI state was last updated.

owner.description: ID of the user who created the UI state (owner of it).

key.description: The key of the UI state. It can be anything really, but it's usually the name of the front-end page for which the state is for.

type.description: The type of the UI state. `presets` is currently the only supported UI state type.

name.description: The name of the UI state.

accessible_by.description: IDs of the users who have access to the UI state. An empty array means that only the owner can access the state. [""] means that all users who can access UI states can access the state.

data.description: The UI state data. It can be any object that front-end wants to store.

data.description:
A JSON-formatted string containing the following information (see sample request payload):

  `command_line`: The command to run.
  `show_window`: Sets whether to display a window on the device. For example, if you run "notepad.exe" with show_window=true, then notepad
  will open in a window. If you run "notepad.exe" with show_window=false, then notepad will run in the background without displaying a window.
  `session_id`: If device_ids contains only a single device, enter the ID of the session to run the command. Otherwise, ignore this parameter.
  The "active_users" field in the "_devices" data index contains a list of active users and their session IDs. See [GET /data/{index_name}](get-data-index) for details.
  `all_users`: If device_ids contains multiple devices, set to true. Otherwise, ignore this parameter.

A JSON-formatted string containing the following information (see sample request payload):

  `script_id`: The ID of the script to run. You can use [GET /scripts](list-all-scripts) to get script IDs. Note that the type of script (user vs. system) determines how you can set the rest of the parameters below.
  `run_as_user`: To run a user script as a single user on a single device, set to true. Otherwise, set to false.
  `run_all_users`: To run a user script as all users on all specified devices, set to true. Otherwise, set to false.
  `run_as_system`: To run a system script on all specified devices, set to true. Otherwise, set to false.
  `session_id`: If you set run_as_user to true, enter the ID of the user session to run the script. If you set run_all_users to true, enter 0. If you set run_as_system to true, set to -1.
  The "active_users" field in the "_devices" data index contains a list of active users and their session IDs. See [GET /data/{index_name}](get-data-index) for details.

builtin_script.description: Indicates if the script is a built-in script.

created.description: When the record was created. This isn't necessarily the time that the survey was completed because there might have been a delay in sending the survey data to the server.

updated.description: When the record was last updated. This isn't relevant for survey results.

type.description: The type of survey result. `Visit` means that the survey was opened. `Start` means that the survey was started. `Result` means that the survey was completed.

survey_dates_type.description: Whether the survey activates according to each device's local time zone (`Local`) or according to UTC (`UTC`). This is relevant only if the survey type is Single or Recurring.

instance_id.description: For recurring surveys, this is the date and time of the survey instance.

device_tags.description: Tags of the device used to access the survey. Returned only for identified surveys.

device_groups.description: Group of the device used to access the survey. Returned only for identified surveys.

device_ds_groups.description: AD groups of the device used to complete the survey. Returned only for identified surveys

user_ds_groups.description: The survey responder's AD groups. Returned only for identified surveys.

started_at.description: For survey completions (type=Result), this is the time when the survey was started.

completed_at.description: For survey completions (type=Result), this is the time when the survey was completed.

time_taken.description: The time taken to complete the survey in milliseconds. Returned only for survey completions.

answers.description: Answers to the questions in the survey. Returned only if the `include_answers` parameter is set to `true`. Note that you can't query the endpoint based on the answers.

type.description: The type of question. This can be `Free Text`, `Single Selection`, `Multiple Selection`, or `Net Promoter Score`.

time_taken.description: Time taken to answer the question in milliseconds.

selection.description: For single selection, multiple selection, or net promoter score questions, this is the ID or IDs of the selected answers. To see which answers correspond to each ID, you can use GET [/user-sentiment/surveys](get-survey).

score.description: For net promoter score questions, this is the score of the option selected. Ranges from 1 to 5.

is_global.description: For net promoter score questions, whether the result from this question contributes to the overall net promoter score for the survey.

text.description: For free text questions, this is the user's response to the question.

score.description: For survey completions (type=Result), the average this is the average score of all Net Promoter Score questions with the Global Net Promoter Score option enabled.

score_raw.description: For survey completions (type=Result), the average this is the average score of all Net Promoter Score questions with the Global Net Promoter Score option enabled.

created.description: When the record was created. This isn't necessarily the time that the survey was completed because there might have been a delay in sending the survey data to the server.

updated.description: When the record was last updated. This isn't relevant for survey answers.

survey_version.description: The version of the Employee Sentiment feature for the survey. For surveys created after April 2024, this is always version 2.

survey_type.description: Survey type. This can be `Single`, `Recurring`, or `Custom Action`.

survey_start_date.description: The start date of the survey.

survey_dates_type.description: Whether the survey activates according to each device's local time zone (`Local`) or according to UTC (`UTC`). This is relevant only if the survey type is Single or Recurring.

is_identified.description: Indicates if the surveys responses are identified (non-anonymous).

instance_id.description: For recurring surveys, this is the date and time of the survey instance.

result_id.description: Result ID. All answers to a survey from a unique user and device have the same result ID.

device_tags.description: Tags of the device used to complete the survey. Returned only for identified surveys.

device_groups.description: Group of the device used to complete the survey. Returned only for identified surveys.

device_ds_groups.description: AD groups of the device used to complete the survey. Returned only for identified surveys.

upn.description: The survey responder's UPN. Returned only for identified surveys.

user_ds_groups.description: The survey responder's AD groups. Returned only for identified surveys.

result_completed_at.description: When the user completed the survey.

type.description: The type of question. This can be `Free Text`, `Single Selection`, `Multiple Selection`, or `Net Promoter Score`.

question_id.description: Question ID. You can use this if you want to find all answers from all users to a specific question. To see more details about the question, you can use GET [/user-sentiment/surveys](get-survey).

time_taken.description: Time taken to answer the question in milliseconds.

selection.description: For single selection, multiple selection, or net promoter score questions, this is the ID or IDs of the selected answers. To see which answers correspond to each ID, you can use GET [/user-sentiment/surveys](get-survey).

text.description: For free text questions, this is the user's response to the question.

is_global.description: For net promoter score questions, whether the result from this question contributes to the overall net promoter score for the survey.

type.description: The type of survey to publish.

status.description: Set to `Scheduled` to publish the survey. Set to `Draft` to save the survey as a draft.

recurring_rule.description:
An [iCalendar Recurrence Rule (RRULE)](https://icalendar.org/iCalendar-RFC-5545/3-8-5-3-recurrence-rule.html) string determining how often the survey repeats and when it ends.

* Example of recurring survey with no end date: `RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO`
* Example of recurring survey with specified end date: `RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO;UNTIL=2025-01-31T03:30:00.000Z`
* Example of recurring survey ending after a specific number of occurences: `RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO;COUNT=5`

retries_days_count.description: The number of days after which a user will stop being reminded to complete the survey. You can set this from 0 to the number of days set in the `instance_duration_days` parameter.

retries_interval.description: The number of hours after a user dismisses the survey until they receive they receive another survey notification.

instance_duration_days.description: Set how long the survey lasts and can be completed after each time it occurs. If the frequency specified in the `recurring_rule` is weekly, `instance_duration_days` can be from 1-6 days. If the frequency specified in the `recurring_rule` is monthly, `instance_duration` can be from 1-21 days.

start_date.description: The starting date and time of the survey in ISO string format.

type.description: The type of survey to publish.

status.description: Set to `Scheduled` to publish the survey. Set to `Draft` to save the survey as a draft.

retries_interval.description: The number of hours after a user dismisses the survey until they receive they receive another survey notification.

start_date.description: The starting date and time of the survey in ISO string format.

expiration_date.description: The end date and time of the survey in ISO string format.

template_id.description: ID of the template from which to create the survey.

dates_type.description: Sets whether the survey scheduling is based on each device's local time zone, or UTC. For example, if you want the survey to appear for each device at 9AM in each time zone, set to `Local`. If you want the survey to appear simultaneously for all devices regardless of their time zones, set to `UTC`.

targeting_type.description:
Sets how survey participants are targeted.
 * If you target `Users`, the survey appears for all users that sign in on a devices. **You must use `included_users` to specify which users to target**. By default the survey appears for the same user multiple times if they sign in from more than one device (you can change this with the `once_per_user` parameter). You might want to target users if more than one employee uses the same device.
 * If you target `Devices`, the survey appears only once for each device. **You must use `included_devices` to specify which devices to target**.

once_per_user.description: If `targeting_type` is set to `Users`, you can set this to `true` so that the survey can be completed by a certain user only once, even if they sign in from multiple devices.

targets_percentage.description: The percentage of targeted users/devices to receive the survey. For example, if you set to 50, then 50% of all users/devices that meet your inclusion and exclusion rules receive the survey (randomly selected).

included_users.description: Applicable and required only if `targeting_type` is set to `Users`. To target all users, set `all` to `true`. Otherwise, set `all` to `false` and use the `directory_services_groups` to target AD groups.

all.description: Sets whether to target all users.

directory_services_groups.description: An array of Active Directory groups to target.

included_devices.description: Applicable and required only if `targeting_type` is set to `Devices`. To target all devices, set `all` to `true`. Otherwise, set `all` to `false` and use the other parameters to specify device targets.

all.description: Sets whether to target all devices.

directory_service_groups.description: An array of Active Directory groups to target.

devices.description: Only applicable if `targeting_type` is set to `Devices`. An array of device names to target.

groups.description: An array of device groups to target.

tags.description: An array of device tags to target,

excluded_devices.description: Devices to exclude from receiving the survey.

directory_services_groups.description: An array of Active Directory groups.

excluded_users.description: Users to exclude from receiving the survey.

directory_services_groups.description: An array of Active Directory groups.

is_identified.description: Sets whether survey participant identities are recorded (non-anonymous).

get.description:
Returns a list of configured alerts.

You can either:
  * Use `query` to use an OpenSearch query. Note that you can't create an OpenSearch query using the request builder built into the documentation.
  * Use the remaining query parameters to query alerts.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: An OpenSearch query.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The number of rows returned per page.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page returned. The number of rows per page is set with the `size` parameter.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The index of the `rows` array to start returning data from. The array index starts at 0. For example, if you set `from` = 2, the first two rows are excluded.

get.description: Returns an alert by its ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the alert to retrieve.

post.description: Edits an existing alert by its ID. Any parameters not passed are unchanged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the alert to edit.

delete.description: Deletes an existing alert by its ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the alert to delete.

post.description:
Returns the content of the specified data index, after applying a filter so that only data from devices within the `device_query` scope is returned.

The endpoint first executes `device_query` against the _devices index to get a list of device IDs. The endpoint then executes `data_query` against the index you specify in the `index` parameter, only returning data that matches the list of device IDs.
For example, you can use this endpoint to search the disk_info data index, but only return data for devices located in New York.

A maximum of 10000 rows can be returned per request. To return more data, you must set `export` to true and use the `_source` parameter to set which fields to return in the data query. For example: `{"data_query":{"_source":["prop1","prop2"]},"export":true}`

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Name of the data index to return.

device_query.description: An OpenSearch query of the _devices data index. Use this query to search for the list of devices to include in the scope for the search of the index specified by the `index` parameter.

data_query.description: An OpenSearch query of the data index specified by the `index` parameter.

404.description: The provided index name is invalid.

get.description: Returns a list of all data indices, along with the size and number of rows in each index.

parameters.name: collapse
parameters.description: Sets whether to collapse weekly data inidices into a single data index. By default, data indices are split into smaller weekly indices so that they are easier to manage. For example, the data index _highresourceprocs_20223400 contains data from the 34th week of 2022 (in UTC).

parameters.name: include_devices
parameters.description: Sets whether to return information about the _devices data index. This is the data index with the columns in the device details grid in the UI.

200.description: An array of data indices. Each entry in the array represents a data index.

name.description: The name of the data index.

size_bytes.description: The size of the data index in bytes.

count.description: The number of documents (rows) in the data index.

get.description:
Retrieves the contents of a data index.

Standard requests can return a maximum of 10000 rows across all pages. For example, if page 1 has 7000 rows, page 2 will be cut off at 3000 rows regardless of the number of rows in the dataset. If you need more rows, set `export`=`true` and use `_source` to specify which fields to include in the export. This method returns up to 65536 rows, or your license count (whichever is greater).

parameters.name: index_name
parameters.description: The name of the index to retrieve.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The number of rows returned per page. The maximum is 10000 rows per page. Read the endpoint description to learn more about the 10000 row limitation.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page returned. The number of rows per page is set with the `size` parameter.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The index of the `rows` array to start returning data from. The array index starts at 0. For example, if you set `from` = 2, the first two rows are excluded.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: Sets whether to return the data index without any pagination, up to 65536 rows or your license count (whichever is greater). You must also use `_source` to specify which fields (columns) to return. `size`, `page`, and `from` parameters will be ignored if true.

parameters.name: _source[0]
parameters.description: If `export`=true, then this parameter sets which field of the data index to return. You can return multiple fields by sending more query parameters and changing the integer in the parameter name (for example, `_source[0]=_device_name&_source[1]=username`).

404.description: The provided index name is invalid.

get.description:
Returns one row for each time a survey was opened, started, or completed. Optionally, use the `include_answers` parameter to also return survey answers.

If you are interested only in returning survey completions (results), you should add a filter to return only rows with `type=Result`. While you can use this endpoint to view all answers in a survey result, you can't query the endpoint based on the answers. To query survey answers, you can use GET [/user-sentiment/results/answers/raw](get-survey-answers).

You can either:
  * Use `query` to use an OpenSearch query. Note that you can't create an OpenSearch query using the request builder built into the documentation.
  * Use the remaining query parameters to query your survey results.
